newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma confirms bomb blast at general's house.
newsitem.headline: Burma confirms bomb blast at general's house.

text.p: Burma's military government on Monday said a bomb had exploded at the house of one of the country's top officials, Lieutenant-General Tin Oo.

"The incident is correct. It is still under consideration and we will send you the details," a government spokesman told Reuters. He would not confirm the reports of sources close to the family that Tin Oo's daughter had died in the blast, but said information on that subject would be issued later.

Sources close to the family of Tin Oo, who is Secretary Two of the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) and Chief of Staff, Army, told Reuters the bomb had killed Tin Oo's eldest daughter.
Witnesses said early on Monday there was tight security near the Medical Hospital Number Two where she was presumably taken.

Burma's military government has been on top security alert since December when two bombs exploded at a Buddhist shrine in Rangoon, killing five and wounding 17. The government blamed the attack on the Karen National Union guerrilla group, which has denied responsibility.

Tin Oo, who is also Chief of Bureau of Special Operations, is one of the hardliners in the SLORC, and often gives speeches urging troops and citizens to "annihilate" anyone who opposes the government or threatens the stability of the nation.
